subject: Private deployment + compliance: HelixCardio discovery recap & RFI
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Mark Trujillo <mark.trujillo@helixcardio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment + compliance: HelixCardio discovery recap & RFI

Hi Mark & Susan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we heard
- HelixCardio is evaluating a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) to meet HIPAA requirements and minimize PHI egress.
- Primary concerns: SOC 2 status, encryption/KMS controls, network isolation, and the feasibility of an air-gapped or limited-egress topology for model inference.
- Timeline: pilot evaluation in Q4 2028, production in early 2029 contingent on compliance signoff and ops readiness.

Immediate asks we discussed
1) HelixCardio to share a coarse network diagram (vpc layout, egress controls, bastion/jump hosts) — we can take a high-level PDF.
2) SOC 2 posture & timelines (Type I/II status, expected completion).
3) Any vendor security questionnaire you prefer (we attached a short RFI template to speed items).

Attachments: vendor_security_rfi.pdf (short template) — please sign/return or mark questions you prefer to answer in a follow-up.

Proposed Redwood next steps
- We will run the RFI internally through Security and Ops to identify any blockers for an on-prem vs VPC approach. (Owners: Marissa + Grace)
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra engineer to walk your network team through integration points (suggested slots below). (Owner: Jonas)
- Prepare an isolation options memo (air-gapped, limited-egress, dedicated subnet) tailored to HelixCardio.

Suggested times for technical deep-dive (PT): Tue Jul 5 10:00–11:00, Wed Jul 6 15:00–16:00, Thu Jul 7 08:00–09:00. Please indicate what works for your infra lead.

Goal for that call: review your diagram, confirm TLS/KMS expectations, and map the minimum required egress for model updates/logging.

If you want, we can redact certain sections of the RFI before sharing with your procurement team — let me know.

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber

Date: 2028-07-01T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment + compliance: HelixCardio discovery recap & RFI

Jonas — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick responses: 

- SOC 2: We completed our SOC 2 Type I in May 2028 and expect a Type II report by Feb 2029 (auditor: BlueLake). We will provide the Type I report and scope summary.
- HIPAA: Confirmed — any PHI workloads must land in our private VPC. We will need formal BAAs in place before production.
- Network diagram: Susan will attach the initial network sketch (coarse) by EOD Monday 2028-07-04. It shows a private subnet for inference, a restricted egress NAT with granular firewall rules, and a separate admin bastion.
- RFI: We'll review your vendor_security_rfi.pdf and have procurement push it back with comments. Happy to take a short questionnaire call vs back-and-forth email.

Can you clarify if Redwood requires outbound connectivity for model artifacts updates, or if the model can be seeded via a staged air-gap process? Also what telemetry/logging options do you support when egress is heavily restricted?

Best — Mark

On Thu, Jul 1, 2028 at 11:30 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Mark & Susan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: ...

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Mark Trujillo <mark.trujillo@helixcardio.com>
Cc: Susan Li <susan.li@helixcardio.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment + compliance: HelixCardio discovery recap & RFI

Mark — thanks, that's helpful. Quick answers and plan: 

Outbound connectivity & model updates
- Short answer: both models are possible. For a purely air-gapped approach we support packaging model artifacts and shipping a signed bundle that your infra can stage locally (no outbound required for inference). This adds a controlled update process and manual steps for model refreshes.
- Alternatively, for a VPC deployment with restricted egress, we support a pull model over TLS to Redwood's artifact endpoint, with client certs and optional IP allowlist. We will document required ports and endpoints in the technical deep-dive.

Telemetry/logging
- With strict egress we can: 1) buffer logs locally and ship via an agent on a schedule, 2) ship only aggregated usage metrics to a customer-owned telemetry endpoint, or 3) write audit logs to an internal S3 bucket that you manage (we can provide the format). We'll detail trade-offs in the memo.

Next actions (agreed)
- HelixCardio: share network sketch (target EOD Mon 2028-07-04). (Owner: HelixCardio - Susan)
- Redwood: provide a short architecture options memo (air-gap vs VPC) and a filled RFI example for your procurement team. (Owners: Marissa + Grace)
- Schedule technical deep-dive once we have the topology. I'll hold the Tue Jul 5 10:00 PT slot tentatively; please confirm.

Attaching: redwood_rfi_instructions.docx (contains guidance on how to return answers and a contacts table).

If it's helpful, please include the network engineer's contact on the next email and we'll send a one-page list of ports/protocols to speed review.

Thanks — Jonas
